entities.summary: Physical chemistry is the study of macroscopic, atomic, subatomic, and particulate phenomena in chemical systems in terms of laws and concepts of physics. Emerging in the 17th century, this field sought to understand the fundamental principles governing chemical reactions and the behavior of matter at the atomic and subatomic level. By applying principles from physics, such as the laws of motion and energy, physical chemists developed new theories and models that explained various chemical phenomena, including chemical reactions, phase transitions, and the properties of materials. The work of pioneers like Antoine Lavoisier, John Dalton, and J.J. Thomson laid the foundation for modern physical chemistry, which has since become a cornerstone of chemistry and a crucial tool for understanding the natural world. As the Industrial Revolution took hold, physical chemists played a key role in the development of new technologies, such as the steam engine and the light bulb, by applying their knowledge of the atomic and subatomic structure of matter to improve efficiency and performance. Today, physical chemistry continues to be a vital area of research, with applications in fields such as materials science, catalysis, and energy storage.
